- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly.
- When sentiment is negative (≤0.33) or volatile, model often underestimates; adjust upward, especially if recent price is falling.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., >5% from prior day), model frequently overshoots; cap forecast at 1–2% below peak or use lagged mean.
- If true outcome shows strong mean reversion (e.g., 3–5 consecutive days below 60), model often fails to correct; apply downward bias of 0.5–1.5 units.
- For 30-day forecasts, model tends to overreact to sentiment shifts; use 7–14 day moving average as baseline for smoothing.
- If sentiment history shows alternating highs/lows (e.g., 0.67, 0.00, 0.67), model often misaligns with true trend; favor sentiment-weighted average over raw forecast.
- When true outcome exceeds forecast by >2.5 units, check if sentiment was bullish 3–5 days prior — if yes, model may be too conservative; increase forecast by 0.5–1.0 units.
